item.title: ShinyHunters PeopleSoft Exploitation, Major Japanese Breaches, and Apple CoreGraphics Patch
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Sep 18:00 → 28 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

ShinyHunters exploiting workarounds for Oracle PeopleSoft bug, Mandiant warns — Must Read

Mandiant warns that ShinyHunters has resumed exploiting Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273, specifically targeting organizations that used workarounds instead of installing Oracle’s patch. The group has compromised dozens of systems globally, deploying web shells and stealing data for extortion.

  • Mandiant warned that ShinyHunters resumed exploiting Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 by targeting organizations that applied workarounds but did not install Oracle’s June 10 patch.
  • Mandiant said the group deployed web shells on dozens of systems globally across higher education, technology, IT services, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, and government.
  • In compromised PeopleSoft systems, ShinyHunters obtained full operating-system control or accessed configuration files, database connection strings, and application data.
  • ShinyHunters claimed it breached an FBI jobs website through an Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability and allegedly stole sensitive FBI data, while FBI officials said they were operating under the premise that employee personal information was also being taken.
  • Mandiant advised PeopleSoft users to review database logs for queries involving human-resources, payroll, and student-record tables and prepare for potential extortion demands.

Products: oracle-peoplesoft

Vendors: oracle, mandiant, google

Apple Patches CoreGraphics Flaw Possibly Exploited in Targeted Attacks — Must Read

Apple patched CVE-2026-86950, a CoreGraphics out-of-bounds write flaw that may have been used in highly sophisticated targeted attacks to execute arbitrary code on older iOS, iPadOS, and macOS versions. Users should update to iOS/iPadOS 26.7.1 or macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and Sequoia 15.8.1.

  • Apple released security updates for older iOS, iPadOS, and macOS versions to address CVE-2026-86950 in CoreGraphics.
  • CVE-2026-86950 is an out-of-bounds write that could enable arbitrary code execution when a device processes a maliciously crafted file.
  • Apple said the flaw may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on iOS versions before iOS 27.
  • The issue was fixed through improved bounds checking and was discovered and reported by Meta Product Security.
  • Apple addressed the flaw in iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1.

Technologies: operating-system, mobile-os

Products: coregraphics, ios, ipados, macos-tahoe, macos-sequoia

Vendors: apple, meta

Over 16,000 Supabase databases expose PII, passwords, auth tokens — Should Read

UpGuard found more than 16,000 misconfigured Supabase databases exposing readable data, including PII, passwords, and authentication tokens, primarily because of weak or missing row-level security and misuse of public keys. The exposures affected organizations worldwide and may be worsened by AI-assisted app development without adequate security review.

  • UpGuard researchers found more than 16,000 misconfigured Supabase databases with publicly readable tables exposing personally identifiable information, passwords, or authentication tokens.
  • The researchers analyzed roughly 300,000 domains that appeared to use Supabase and used accessible table schemas to infer the kinds of data exposed.
  • More than half of the exposed databases contained personally identifiable information, while smaller subsets included passwords and authentication tokens.
  • Examples included a U.S. valet service exposing over 100,000 customer records and a Canadian immigration service exposing nearly 5,000 user records, including 884 plaintext passwords.
  • UpGuard attributed the exposures to poor application security settings, including missing or ineffective row-level security policies and misuse of public keys.

Technologies: database, cloud-platform

Products: supabase, postgresql

Vendors: supabase, upguard

Times Car confirms data breach affecting 6.6 million user accounts — Should Read

Japanese car-sharing provider Times Car confirmed that a cyberattack exposed personal data from roughly 6.6 million current and former members, including driver’s license and identity-verification documents. Credit card data was not affected, and the company says passwords were stored in a non-reversible form.

  • Times Car confirmed that unauthorized access to its systems resulted in the theft of data affecting approximately 6.6 million current and former members, including members of its Times Business Service corporate program.
  • The exposed information includes names, addresses, birth dates, telephone numbers, email addresses, driver’s license information, identity-verification document images, account passwords, and linked service IDs.
  • Times Car said the affected passwords were stored in a form that cannot be restored, while credit card information was not affected.
  • The company said it has no evidence that the stolen data has been distributed online and is conducting a forensic investigation with an external expert.
  • Times Car will notify affected customers in stages and has warned members to be cautious of emails, SMS messages, and phone calls claiming to come from the company.

Products: times-car, times-business-service

Vendors: times-mobility, park24-group

Hackers Use NeedyMantis to Maintain Long-Term Access in Breached Networks — Should Read

Microsoft says the NeedyMantis malware family is being used in targeted post-compromise intrusions to maintain long-term access through DLL sideloading and encrypted payloads. The activity, including use by the suspected China-linked Storm-3069 group, has targeted organizations across telecommunications, academia, healthcare, intergovernmental bodies, and government contracting.

  • Microsoft identified NeedyMantis as a malware family used to maintain long-term access in a small number of targeted intrusions affecting telecommunications organizations, universities, medical nonprofits, intergovernmental organizations, and government contractors.
  • NeedyMantis commonly uses DLL sideloading, packaging a legitimate application with a malicious DLL and encrypted archive so that the application loads and runs the malware.
  • Microsoft tracks one user of NeedyMantis as Storm-3069, assesses its activity appears to originate in China, and has not attributed it to a Chinese nation-state actor.
  • Microsoft has not confirmed that NeedyMantis was distributed through the compromised DAEMON Tools Lite installers, although it found the malware while investigating indicators related to that supply-chain incident.
  • Microsoft published file hashes, a command-and-control domain, file paths, and hunting queries to help defenders identify NeedyMantis activity.

Technologies: antivirus, edr, xdr, siem, remote-access

Products: daemon-tools-lite, microsoft-defender-antivirus, microsoft-defender-xdr, microsoft-sentinel, poedit, tightvnc

Vendors: microsoft, kaspersky, google, mandiant

Japan's Keio confirms ransomware attack disrupted business systems — Should Read

Keio Corporation confirmed a ransomware attack that disrupted hospitality business systems and payment services, while train operations appear unaffected. The company is investigating possible data exposure with outside experts and police.

  • Keio Corporation confirmed that its group servers were hit by a ransomware attack in the early hours of September 26, 2026.
  • Keio shut down its network to limit further damage and is investigating the attack route, impact, and whether customer or business-partner information was accessed.
  • The incident appears to affect Keio’s hospitality operations and may have disrupted payment systems, while train operations were not affected.
  • Tokyo Metro separately reported unauthorized access to systems containing 59,000 member email addresses and said it had identified and closed the weakness used.
  • No ransomware group had publicly claimed responsibility for the Keio incident at the time of reporting.

Dutch police confirm arrest in ShinyHunters hacking investigation — Should Read

Dutch police confirmed that a 24-year-old Amsterdam man was arrested in an investigation into ShinyHunters, though the group denies he has any connection to it. The suspect, reportedly former hacker Pepijn van der Stap (“Umbreon”), was already on probation for prior hacking and extortion convictions.

  • Dutch police confirmed that a 24-year-old Amsterdam man was arrested this month as part of an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group.
  • The suspect is scheduled to appear before the Rotterdam District Court on September 29, when police said more information will be released.
  • KrebsOnSecurity and DataBreaches identified the suspect as Pepijn van der Stap, previously known online as “Umbreon,” who was convicted in an earlier hacking and blackmail case.
  • Dutch tactical police searched the Amsterdam home van der Stap shared with his mother on September 15 and seized electronic devices, according to DataBreaches.
  • A ShinyHunters representative denied that van der Stap has any association with the group.

IAM for AI agents: A Practical Enterprise Framework — Optional

Enterprise IAM for AI agents must go beyond provisioning and static roles by assigning distinct, owned, short-lived identities and enforcing task-scoped permissions. Organizations also need runtime observability across applications and infrastructure to verify what agents actually did and rapidly revoke authority when behavior exceeds intent.

  • AI agents should be treated as non-human identities with a human owner, defined purpose, scoped authorization, expiration, and continuous monitoring.
  • Traditional IAM systems show configured access and authentication events but generally do not show what an autonomous agent did inside an application.
  • Agent identities should use distinct identities and favor federated workload identity with short-lived, automatically rotated credentials instead of embedded secrets.
  • Task-scoped grants, tool allowlists, data boundaries, and approval requirements for high-consequence actions can constrain agent behavior.
  • Organizations need application- and infrastructure-level telemetry to compare an agent’s intended task with its actual execution and support rapid revocation when they diverge.

Technologies: iam, identity-provider

Products: orchid-security

Vendors: orchid-security, sailpoint, saviynt

item.title: Actively Exploited Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 Drive Urgent Patching
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Sep 14:00 → 28 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Threat Brief: NetScaler Zero Days CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 Exploited in the Wild — Must Read

Citrix reports that two critical NetScaler ADC and Gateway zero-days, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, are being exploited in the wild and can enable unauthenticated remote code execution or denial of service. Organizations should urgently identify exposed appliances, preserve forensic evidence, investigate for compromise, isolate vulnerable systems, and apply Citrix updates.

  • Citrix reports that CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway have been exploited in the wild.
  • CVE-2026-88771 is an input-validation flaw that can allow an unauthenticated actor to run commands on affected NetScaler systems.
  • CVE-2026-88772 is a DTLS-related memory-overflow flaw that can result in remote code execution or denial of service.
  • Both CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 have a CVSS v4.0 base score of 9.5.
  • As of September 27, 2026, Cortex Xpanse identified more than 50,277 exposed instances potentially vulnerable to these CVEs based on Palo Alto Networks telemetry.

Technologies: load-balancer, remote-access, vpn

Products: netscaler-adc, netscaler-gateway, cortex-xpanse

Vendors: citrix, palo-alto-networks

JadePuffer agentic AI attacks target Azure, destroy cloud resources — Should Read

Microsoft observed JadePuffer (Storm-3168) using compromised Azure service principals to rapidly map cloud environments, steal storage keys, and delete storage accounts and other resources. Resource locks and account protections blocked some destructive actions, while one exposed credential may have appeared in a public GitHub issue.

  • Microsoft observed two June attacks in which JadePuffer, tracked as Storm-3168, used compromised Azure service principals to discover cloud resources, collect credentials, and delete Azure Storage accounts.
  • The destructive activity lasted seven minutes and targeted more than 100 storage accounts as well as Azure Key Vaults, Function Apps, virtual machines, and App Services.
  • Azure resource locks and storage-account protections prevented the deletion of some targeted storage accounts, while attempts to delete Azure SQL databases and recovery protection locks failed.
  • About 30 minutes after the deletion attempts, Storm-3168 made more than 30 requests for storage account keys, most of which succeeded.
  • Microsoft could not determine the initial access method, but said credentials for one of the compromised service principals appeared in a public GitHub issue before the attacks.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, secrets-manager, backup, database

Products: microsoft-azure, azure-storage, azure-key-vault, azure-site-recovery, azure-sql-database, azure-functions, azure-virtual-machines, azure-app-service

Vendors: microsoft, sysdig, github

No Passwords, No Customer Data, Still a Problem — Should Read

Threat actor TheHatman advertised millions of apparently genuine corporate directory records allegedly taken from Azure and Entra environments, though evidence does not confirm recent breaches of the named organizations. Even without passwords or customer data, directory information enables highly convincing phishing and impersonation, underscoring the need to restrict and monitor identity and application access to Microsoft Graph and directory data.

  • Between July 31 and August 16, TheHatman posted underground listings claiming to offer about 3.64 million employee records from nine organizations, allegedly obtained from Microsoft Azure and Entra environments.
  • Cyera Research found that sample records appeared to contain genuine corporate directory data, including names, work email addresses, telephone numbers, job titles, locations, group memberships, service accounts, and privileged accounts.
  • The available evidence does not establish when or where the records were obtained, whether TheHatman personally compromised the named organizations, or whether nine separate cloud environments were breached.
  • TCS, Gap, and Vodafone disputed indications of recent compromises, with TCS saying the material appeared to be more than four years old and Vodafone saying customer data was not affected.
  • Directory information can help criminals tailor phishing, executive impersonation, and identity-recovery scams, so organizations should review directory-read access and investigate unusual bulk directory-enumeration activity.

Technologies: cloud-platform, identity-provider, iam

Products: microsoft-azure, microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-graph

Vendors: microsoft, cyera

New Mexico jury finds Meta deceived consumers about data privacy practices — Should Read

A New Mexico jury found Facebook/Meta violated the state’s consumer-protection law nearly 44 million times by deceptively representing its data privacy, content-moderation, and third-party app practices. A judge will determine penalties, which could reach billions of dollars, along with potential mandated privacy reforms.

  • A New Mexico jury found that Facebook violated the state’s Unfair Practices Act nearly 44 million times by deceiving consumers about its data privacy practices.
  • The jury determined that Facebook misled users about their control over information sharing and about whether it bought or sold users’ private data, particularly with advertisers.
  • Jurors found Facebook’s statements concerning hate speech, misinformation, and adherence to its community standards were willfully deceptive.
  • The jury also found that Facebook did not fulfill promises to investigate third-party applications that accessed substantial user data after the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
  • A judge will determine Meta’s penalties in coming weeks, and New Mexico is seeking both civil fines and sweeping changes to Facebook’s future data privacy practices.

Products: facebook

Vendors: meta

Aikido funds Node.js security — May Read

Aikido Security has joined the OpenJS Foundation’s Security Stewardship Program to fund Node.js vulnerability bounties and maintainer remediation support. The initiative aims to address declining bounty resources and the growing burden of low-quality AI-generated reports on open-source maintainers.

  • Aikido has joined the OpenJS Foundation’s Security Stewardship Program as an inaugural partner, initially funding work related to Node.js.
  • The program splits its funding evenly between rewards for researchers who find security flaws and direct support for maintainers who deliver fixes.
  • OpenJS will handle report review and CVE coordination, reducing the administrative burden on maintainers.
  • Node.js ended its security bug bounty program after Internet Bug Bounty funding ended, while AI-generated low-quality reports have increased pressure on maintainers.
  • Aikido says its support is intended to help researchers and maintainers keep the Node.js ecosystem secure.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: node-js, npm, drydock, aikido-intel, composer

Vendors: aikido-security, openjs-foundation, node-js, curl, github, drydock, composer, packagist

80,000+ Organizations Had AI Logins Stolen: From Shadow AI to LLMjacking — Optional

SOCRadar reports that infostealer logs contain stolen AI-platform credentials or sessions tied to more than 80,000 corporate domains, exposing chat histories, API keys, automation access, and billable AI resources. Organizations should discover shadow AI accounts, invalidate compromised sessions, enforce SSO, and monitor API-key misuse.

  • SOCRadar analyzed more than one million infostealer records tied to AI services across over 80,000 corporate domains and closely examined 482 major enterprises.
  • The 482 enterprises had 5,434 stealer-log records tied to 1,500 distinct corporate email addresses, with 295 organizations appearing in records from the previous 90 days.
  • ChatGPT or OpenAI sessions appeared at 358 of the 482 companies and accounted for roughly 90% of the records in the study.
  • Stolen AI sessions can expose conversation histories, bypass password-based authentication, enable misuse of connected automation services, and allow attackers to consume or resell API access.
  • The article recommends identifying unapproved AI accounts, using single sign-on with short-lived sessions, rotating and limiting API keys, and investigating employees found in stealer logs as endpoint incidents.

Products: ai-identity-exposure-checker, claude, chatgpt, gemini, hugging-face, replit, zapier, notion, lovable, elevenlabs, cursor

Vendors: socradar, anthropic, openai, hugging-face, replit, zapier, notion, lovable, elevenlabs, cursor

item.title: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 Exploitation and Carbonato Docker Botnet Activity
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Sep 10:00 → 28 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Oh Look, The Foot Gun Went Off Again (Citrix NetScaler PreAuth Command Injection CVE-2026-88771) — Must Read

Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 is an actively exploited, pre-authentication command injection affecting default configurations, allowing remote attackers to execute commands as root through poisoned log entries. Organizations should urgently update NetScaler ADC and Gateway to Citrix’s fixed releases.

  • CVE-2026-88771 is a pre-authentication command-injection flaw in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway that Citrix says was exploited in the wild and affects default configurations.
  • The vulnerable NetScaler script ns_monuploadd_err.pl extracted attacker-influenced text from logs and inserted it into a shell command, enabling arbitrary commands to run as root.
  • The article states that controlled values in login fields, request parameters, HTTP headers, failed login attempts, and rate-limited requests can reach logs and potentially trigger the issue.
  • Citrix fixed the flaw by restricting extracted core-file values to a Packet Engine name and numeric process ID, invoking find without a shell, and validating returned paths.
  • Citrix recommends updating NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1 to version 14.1-73.37 or later, and 13.1 to version 13.1-64.23 or later.

Technologies: load-balancer, vpn, remote-access

Products: citrix-netscaler-adc, citrix-netscaler-gateway, watchtowr-platform

Vendors: citrix, watchtowr

Cyberattack on Polish medical software provider exposes patient data — Should Read

Polish medical software provider Qbusoft suffered an SQL injection breach of its Medyc platform, potentially exposing patient identities and sensitive medical records. Authorities are investigating amid broader attacks on Poland’s healthcare sector, while attackers claim to have stolen data on millions of patients.

  • Qbusoft’s Medyc healthcare platform was breached after an attacker exploited an SQL injection flaw in August, with the intrusion detected overnight on September 9.
  • Attackers obtained names, PESEL national identification numbers, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses, while medical-record theft has not been confirmed but is considered highly likely by an affected provider.
  • Patients of the Addiction and Psychiatric Treatment Center in Inowrocław’s Day Treatment Unit for Addiction Treatment were affected, and potentially exposed records included hospital treatment documentation and discharge summaries.
  • Qbusoft said it fixed the flaw on the day the incident was discovered, restricted database permissions, rotated credentials, and added monitoring.
  • Polish authorities are investigating the incident, and the data protection authority has ordered an audit of the company behind Medyc.

Technologies: database

Products: medyc, mydr

Vendors: qbusoft, mydr

Carbonato Botnet Compromises Docker Hosts to Deploy Telegram-Controlled Hermes AI Agent — Should Read

The Carbonato botnet exploits unauthenticated Docker daemons to worm across networks, establish persistent remote access, and deploy a Telegram-controlled Hermes AI agent that can execute attacker-directed commands and steal credentials.

  • Carbonato targets Docker daemons exposed without authentication on port 2375, launches privileged containers on compromised hosts, and scans nearby networks every five minutes to spread further.
  • The botnet installs Hermes Agent, replaces its SOUL.md persona with instructions to accept Telegram tasks, maintain persistence, and prioritize collecting AI API keys and other credentials.
  • Carbonato creates a reverse SSH tunnel to a relay in Costa Rica, installs an SSH server using the operators' key, and reports new deployments through Telegram.
  • The malware masquerades as a system component and uses cron jobs and watchdog scripts to restart itself if its files are removed.
  • The report links Carbonato to a broader trend of attackers using AI agents and large language models to automate target discovery, exploitation, post-compromise activity, and command-and-control.

Technologies: container-platform, remote-access

Products: hermes-agent, docker-engine, telegram, claude-opus-4-6, deepseek-v4-1-flash, qwen, gemini

Vendors: nous-research, docker, telegram, anthropic, deepseek, alibaba, mistral, google

Former US soldier gets nearly six-year sentence for hacking, extorting telecoms — Should Read

Former U.S. Army soldier Cameron John Wagenius was sentenced to 70 months in prison and ordered to pay nearly $295,000 for hacking telecoms, stealing sensitive customer records, and extorting victims. Prosecutors said he also tried to sell stolen data to a foreign military intelligence service.

  • Former U.S. Army soldier Cameron John Wagenius, 22, received a 70-month federal prison sentence and was ordered to pay nearly $295,000 in restitution.
  • Wagenius pleaded guilty to wire fraud, extortion, aggravated identity theft, and charges related to posting and transmitting confidential phone records.
  • Between April 2023 and December 2024, Wagenius and two other hackers stole sensitive call records and other customer data from telecommunications companies and sought at least $1 million in ransoms.
  • Using the username "kiberphant0m," Wagenius used a tool called "SSH Brute" with others to access at least 10 organizations and market stolen data on BreachForums and XSS.is.
  • Prosecutors said Wagenius contacted an address he believed belonged to an unnamed country’s military intelligence service in an attempt to sell stolen information.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: snowflake

Vendors: snowflake, at-t, t-mobile

A Salary Notice Whose Effective Date Was Its Build Clock — May Read

A payroll phishing PDF exposed its automated generation by using a salary effective timestamp one second before the file was created and two seconds before delivery. Although the attachment contained no malicious links or code, its QR-code signing prompt and broken personalization made it a social-engineering lure that was caught by human reporting.

  • A fake payroll PDF stated that a compensation adjustment was effective at 2026-05-07 11:50:13, while its creation timestamp was one second later and the email was timestamped at 11:50:15 UTC.
  • Four mailboxes at a UAE-based food import and distribution group received the messages within about four minutes, and all four were quarantined.
  • The PDF used the recipient's email address for both the employee identification and document reference fields, and addressed a shared mailbox local part as though it were a person.
  • The attachment instructed recipients to scan a verification code to electronically sign documentation, but analysis found no PDF links, scripts, automatic actions, recovered code, or destination.
  • The attachment was readable and contained no executable content, so the platform scan correctly marked it clean; a human report led to the malicious verdict.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: ironscales-platform, qt, wkhtmltopdf

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, qt-project

Attack Surface Management in 2026: Why Point-in-Time Scans Can’t Keep Up With Cloud Sprawl — Optional

Quarterly or annual attack-surface scans cannot keep pace with rapidly changing cloud environments, leaving ephemeral and misconfigured internet-facing assets unmonitored for extended periods. The article argues that continuous outside-in discovery, monitoring, prioritization, and ownership workflows are now necessary, and promotes Cyble Odin as a solution.

  • Point-in-time attack-surface scans become outdated within hours in multi-cloud environments driven by infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, and self-service provisioning.
  • Ephemeral assets, decentralized ownership, and configuration drift can create unmonitored external exposures between scheduled scan windows.
  • CISA Binding Operational Directive 23-01 requires U.S. federal civilian agencies to perform automated asset discovery every seven days and vulnerability enumeration every 14 days.
  • ENISA reported that vulnerability exploitation accounted for 21.3% of initial access in the EU in 2025, with widespread campaigns weaponizing flaws within days of disclosure.
  • The article states that continuous attack surface management requires outside-in discovery, continuous monitoring, threat-informed prioritization, and ownership workflows.

Products: cyble-attack-surface-management, cyble-odin

Vendors: cyble

Webinar: How to Govern AI Agents, Reduce Excessive Access, and Control Shadow AI — Optional

Okta is hosting a webinar on treating AI agents as first-class identities to improve visibility, ownership, access reviews, and revocation. The session focuses on reducing excessive permissions and governing shadow AI rather than simply blocking it.

  • Okta is hosting a webinar with Regional CSO Matt Immler on governing AI agents as first-class identities.
  • Okta’s Global CISO Insights 2026 report found that only 47% of CISOs are confident they can identify every AI agent in their environment.
  • The article states that only one in four surveyed organizations has adopted a purpose-built framework for securing AI agents, while 21% still use shared credentials or broad-permission service accounts.
  • The webinar will address discovering AI agents, assigning ownership, reviewing their access, reducing excessive permissions, and controlling shadow AI.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam

Vendors: okta

item.title: Actively Exploited Citrix NetScaler CVEs and Bitget’s $387.5 Million North Korean Heist
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Sep 06:00 → 28 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA orders feds to patch exploited Citrix flaws by Wednesday — Must Read

CISA ordered U.S. federal agencies to patch two actively exploited critical Citrix NetScaler RCE zero-days, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, by September 30. Organizations with internet-facing NetScaler appliances should assess for compromise and preserve evidence before patching where possible.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and ordered U.S. federal civilian agencies to secure vulnerable Citrix appliances by September 30.
  • Citrix confirmed that both NetScaler vulnerabilities are being actively exploited and urged affected customers to install updated versions immediately.
  • The flaws can allow unauthenticated attackers to run code remotely on vulnerable NetScaler appliances; CVE-2026-88772 requires DTLS to be enabled.
  • CISA advised organizations to check for signs of compromise and preserve forensic evidence before patching where possible, because updates may reduce forensic visibility.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 23,000 internet-exposed IP addresses with NetScaler fingerprints, although it is unknown how many are patched, vulnerable, or honeypots.

Technologies: load-balancer, vpn, network-monitoring

Products: netscaler-adc, netscaler-gateway, netscaler-console

Vendors: citrix

Bitget resumes Bitcoin withdrawals after $387.5 million crypto heist — Must Read

Bitget resumed Bitcoin withdrawals after a suspected North Korean-linked breach of its wallet infrastructure led to the theft of approximately $387.5 million in crypto assets. The exchange says the flaw has been fixed, user balances are covered by its Protection Fund, and withdrawals for other assets will be restored on a phased schedule.

  • Bitget resumed Bitcoin withdrawals after suspending all withdrawals following unauthorized transfers from a limited number of its crypto wallets.
  • Bitget said its latest on-chain tracing and transaction classification found that $387.5 million was transferred to attacker-controlled addresses.
  • Bitget CEO Gracy Chen attributed the incident to North Korean hackers who allegedly breached a critical backend system in Bitget’s wallet infrastructure and spoofed transaction data.
  • Bitget said user account balances remain unaffected, its Protection Fund covers the financial impact, and trading and deposits continue to operate.
  • The exchange plans to resume withdrawals for Ethereum-related networks on September 29, selected USDT networks on September 30, and other tokens, fiat, and P2P assets beginning October 2.

Products: bitget

Vendors: bitget

US soldier gets 70 months in prison for extorting 10 tech, telecom firms — May Read

Former U.S. Army soldier Cameron John Wagenius was sentenced to 70 months in prison and ordered to pay nearly $295,000 for hacking and extorting at least 10 U.S. technology and telecom companies, including AT&T and Verizon. The scheme used stolen credentials and threats to leak data, with attempted extortion totaling at least $1 million.

  • Former U.S. Army soldier Cameron John Wagenius was sentenced to 70 months in prison for hacking and extorting at least 10 U.S. technology and telecommunications companies between April 2023 and December 2024.
  • Wagenius and his accomplices used stolen network login credentials, including credentials obtained with the SSH Brute tool, and coordinated through Telegram.
  • The group threatened to publish stolen data on BreachForums and XSS.is or sold it for thousands of dollars, while attempting to extort at least $1 million from victim data owners.
  • Wagenius was ordered to pay $294,978 in restitution for accessing sensitive telecom customer records and extorting companies under threats to release stolen data.
  • The article links two alleged accomplices, Connor Riley Moucka and John Erin Binns, to thefts of data from more than 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage services.

Technologies: cloud-platform, database

Products: snowflake

Vendors: snowflake

How Data Lineage Catches a File That’s Trying Not to Be Found — Optional

Netskope promotes its One Data Lineage capability, which combines inline, SaaS API, and endpoint telemetry to trace files even after local renames and edits break traditional filename, hash, and application-ID matching.

  • Files often lose stable identifiers as they move between applications and devices because application IDs, filenames, and content hashes can change after downloads, edits, renames, and uploads.
  • Netskope One Data Lineage ranks evidence by strength, favoring events that identify both a source and destination, then shared application object IDs, content matches under limited conditions, and finally name, location, and time correlations.
  • The product deliberately avoids treating matching content alone as proof that a file moved and keeps uncertain connections visually distinct from proven lineage.
  • Netskope combines inline network activity, SaaS API connector activity, and endpoint events to construct file lineage.
  • Endpoint events can record local file creation, editing, renaming, copying, deletion, and transfers through browsers, USB drives, network shares, or Bluetooth, helping link network events that otherwise appear unrelated.

Technologies: dlp, casb

Products: netskope-one-data-lineage, microsoft-sharepoint, google-drive

Vendors: netskope, microsoft, google

item.title: OpenAI Reportedly Tests “o” Always-On ChatGPT Assistant With Email Capability
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Citrix Confirms Exploited NetScaler CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 Zero-Days
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Sep 14:00 → 27 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Citrix confirms two NetScaler RCE zero-days exploited in attacks — Must Read

Citrix confirmed that two critical NetScaler RCE zero-days, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, are actively being exploited and released patches for affected ADC and Gateway appliances. Organizations should urgently upgrade to the fixed builds or reduce Internet exposure until patching is possible.

  • Citrix confirmed that CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, two critical NetScaler remote code execution flaws with severity scores of 9.5, have been exploited as zero-days.
  • CVE-2026-88771 affects all NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway deployments, including default configurations, and lets an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary commands because of improper input validation.
  • CVE-2026-88772 can enable remote code execution or denial of service when DTLS is enabled, which Citrix says is enabled by default on VPN virtual servers.
  • Citrix released patches for affected NetScaler ADC and Gateway versions, while Secure Private Access Hybrid deployments using NetScaler instances must also be upgraded to recommended builds.
  • The Dutch National Cyber Security Center reportedly warned organizations before public disclosure that exploitation had been identified at multiple Citrix customers worldwide.

Technologies: vpn, load-balancer, remote-access

Products: netscaler-adc, netscaler-gateway, secure-private-access-hybrid, adaptive-authentication

Vendors: citrix, cloud-software-group

Cloudflare fixes Containers cross-tenant flaw exposing customer data — Should Read

Cloudflare fixed a cross-tenant storage flaw in its Containers and Sandboxes service that could have let paid Workers users recover residual data from other customers’ deleted container disks. Cloudflare says it completed mitigations, found no evidence of real-world exposure, and customers need take no action.

  • Cloudflare fixed a flaw in its Containers and Sandboxes service that could have allowed Workers Paid customers to recover residual data from other customers’ containers on the same physical host.
  • The issue arose because reused 64 KiB storage blocks were not fully cleared before being reassigned, leaving up to 60 KiB of prior data readable after a 4 KiB write.
  • Researchers reported the flaw through HackerOne on September 4 and found residual material on 18 of 24 container placements across 20 of 22 underlying nodes tested.
  • Cloudflare removed the configuration that skipped clearing reused blocks, retired existing container disks, and cleared cached snapshots by September 19, 2026.
  • Cloudflare said the researchers collected only aggregate test results rather than disk contents and that its review found no evidence of customer data exposure through this method.

Technologies: container-platform, cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-containers, cloudflare-workers, cloudflare-sandboxes

Vendors: cloudflare, accomplish

item.title: Claude Marketplace Launch and Google Calendar Redirect Phishing Evasion
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Sep 10:00 → 27 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Google Calendar Phishing: One Link, Two Scanner Verdicts — Should Read

Attackers abused Google Calendar to send a fully authenticated phishing invite containing a Google redirect link to a domain registered only 29 minutes earlier, causing URL scanners to rate the trusted wrapper clean while the underlying destination received only a partial warning. The incident shows that email defenses must resolve and assess final destinations rather than trust platform redirectors or sender authentication.

  • An attacker placed a voicemail lure in a Google Calendar event description and invited a VIP mailbox at a digital advertising group, prompting Google to send an authenticated calendar notification.
  • The malicious destination voiceml[.]space was registered 29 minutes and 26 seconds before Google sent the notification, and the bare URL received a partial "Mixed Result" scanner verdict.
  • Google Calendar rewrote the lure link through a google.com redirector, which was scanned as clean even though its q parameter led to the same destination.
  • SPF, DKIM, and DMARC all passed because the message was genuinely sent by Google Calendar rather than forged by the attacker.
  • The recipient reported the suspicious message, and the message was mitigated after a human manual approval recorded the malicious finding.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform, proxy

Products: google-calendar, google-workspace, ironscales-themis

Vendors: google, ironscales, cloudflare, namecheap

Anthropic turns Claude into an AI marketplace with 2,000+ plugins and connectors — Optional

Anthropic launched the Claude Marketplace with more than 2,000 plugins, connectors, agents, and consulting offerings, aiming to make Claude a central platform for third-party AI integrations and products.

  • Anthropic has launched a public Claude Marketplace offering more than 2,000 connectors and plugins.
  • The marketplace includes integrations from companies including Atlassian, Google, Microsoft, Notion, and Salesforce.
  • Companies can buy Claude-powered agents and products from partners such as CrowdStrike, Cursor, Harvey, Legora, Lovable, and Snowflake.
  • Developers can build and publish Claude connectors and plugins using Model Context Protocol and Agent Skills.
  • The marketplace also lists consulting and systems integration partners, including Accenture, Boston Consulting Group, and Deloitte, for organizations deploying Claude.

item.title: Two Unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE Zero-Days Reportedly Under Active Exploitation
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Sep 06:00 → 27 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Frequently asked questions about reported Citrix NetScaler zero-day vulnerabilities — Must Read

Reports indicate two unpatched Citrix NetScaler zero-days enabling remote code execution are being actively exploited, but Citrix had not yet issued CVEs, an advisory, patches, or public indicators of compromise as of September 27, 2026.

  • Public reports indicated that two unpatched Citrix NetScaler zero-day flaws capable of remote code execution were being actively exploited in the wild.
  • As of September 27, 2026, Citrix had not published a formal security advisory, assigned CVE identifiers, or released patches for the reported flaws.
  • The reported zero-days were not believed to be related to CVE-2026-19490 or CVE-2026-19489, which were previously disclosed Citrix NetScaler vulnerabilities with patches available.
  • No public proof-of-concept code, indicators of compromise, or details identifying the responsible threat actors were available as of September 27, 2026.
  • Citrix NetScaler devices have been frequent targets historically, with 13 NetScaler-related entries in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of September 27, 2026.

Technologies: load-balancer, vpn, remote-access

Products: netscaler-adc, netscaler-gateway

Vendors: citrix
